newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee untraded, dealers mark time.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee untraded, dealers mark time.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was unmoved against the dollar nearly two hours after the market opened due to dealers not willing to create positions, and a lack of early commercial demand.
At 0445 GMT the rupee remained quoted at its opening level of 56.78. The rupee closed at the same level on Thursday.
"No one wants to create new positions this close to the end of the year," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
There was no early import-covering demand either, he said.
The Central Bank left the exchange rate unchanged, and buying and selling rates remained at 56.1206 and 57.2544.
Most of the early activity was seen in the overnight call money market, where rates rose to 21 percent after opening at 16, dealers said.
"The rise was not necessary because the market is liquid. But banks panicked when they saw money at 16 percent, which pushed the rate up to 21," said an ABN Amro dealer.
A non-banking institution which came on with a big lending positions, brought call money down to 18 percent, he said.
